llmsa: Measurement System Analysis for Pipelines Built on Large Language Models

Kurzfassung. llmsa behandelt eine Auswertungspipeline, die auf einem Sprachmodell aufsetzt, als das, was sie ist: ein Messverfahren mit unbekannter Messunsicherheit. Das Paket validiert sie mit den Methoden, die analytische und klinische Labore seit Jahrzehnten verwenden: gekreuzte Präzisionsstudie mit Varianzkomponenten (Gage R&R), Attribut-Übereinstimmung mit Kappa-Statistiken, Richtigkeit gegen eine Referenz, Plackett-Burman-Screening der Robustheit, Fallzahlplanung per Simulation, Regelkarten mit Westgard-Regeln für die laufende Systemeignung und ein prüffähiger Validierungsbericht. Es ist unabhängig vom verwendeten Modell und von der Pipeline selbst.

Why

Benchmarks report how often a model is right. A laboratory needs to know something else before it acts on a result: how much the result changes when the same question is asked again (repeatability), when it is asked differently or of another model (reproducibility), whether it is systematically off (bias), whether a typo or a different number format changes it (robustness), and whether it is still behaving the same way next month (system suitability). None of this is new. Measurement system analysis (AIAG MSA), CLSI EP05, ICH Q2(R2) and Westgard rules answer exactly these questions for instruments. llmsa applies them to pipelines built on large language models, whose endpoints are not deterministic even at temperature 0 and whose models change silently.

The result is a validation report in the structure a reviewer or an auditor expects, which is also what the FDA’s 2025 draft guidance on AI in regulatory decision-making asks for: a credibility assessment tied to a stated context of use and model risk.

What maps to what

Measurement system analysis LLM pipeline
Part Item (variant, document, assay record)
Appraiser Prompt variant (semantically equivalent wording)
Instrument Model (provider, version, quantisation)
Trial / replicate Repeated call under identical conditions
Day / session Block (endpoints drift with load and time)
Repeatability Variance between replicate calls
Reproducibility Variance from prompt, model, block and their interactions
Part-to-part variation Variance between items, the signal to resolve
Reference standard Expert-curated answer
Robustness (ICH Q2) Plackett-Burman screening of formatting and context perturbations
Control sample Small set with known answers, run before each batch

Installation 

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("DanielMoj/llmsa", build_vignettes = TRUE)

Dependencies are lme4 and ordinal. Reports need rmarkdown and pandoc; backends need httr2 or ellmer.

Quick start 

library(llmsa)

# 1. items (parts), prompt variants (appraisers), models (instruments)
items <- data.frame(item_id = c("v1", "v2", "v3"),
                    text = c("NM_000059.4:c.1813dupA", "NM_000059.4:c.7397T>C", "NM_000059.4:c.68-7T>A"),
                    reference = c("Pathogenic", "Benign", "VUS"))
tiers <- c("Benign", "Likely benign", "VUS", "Likely pathogenic", "Pathogenic")
prompts <- c(concise = "Classify {text} (ACMG/AMP five tiers). Answer with the tier only.",
             role    = "You are a clinical geneticist. Give the ACMG/AMP tier of {text}.")
design <- msa_design(items, prompts, models = c("gpt-4.1", "qwen3:8b"), reps = 3, blocks = 2, seed = 1)

# 2. run against any backend, with an audit trail
backend <- backend_openai_compatible("http://localhost:11434/v1", api_key = "")   # Ollama
runs <- msa_run(design, backend, parse = parse_choice(tiers), store = "runs.sqlite")

# 3. precision, agreement, robustness, report
fit <- msa_fit(runs, type = "ordinal", levels = tiers)
grr <- msa_grr(fit)                      # %GRR, ndc, verdict
ag  <- msa_agreement(runs, levels = tiers, reference = "reference", weights = "linear")
msa_report(grr, runs = runs, agreement = ag,
           cou = "Pre-classification of sequence variants for expert review",
           risk = "medium", acceptance = "%GRR < 30 %; kappa (modal) >= 0.8",
           output_file = "validation_report.html")

Results produced by another pipeline (Python, a workflow engine, a spreadsheet) are analysed the same way after as_msa_runs().

g <- msa_grr(msa_fit(ic50_demo, type = "numeric"))
g

Functions

Step Function
Plan a crossed study msa_design()
Run it with an audit trail, resume after interruption msa_run(), backend_mock(), backend_ellmer(), backend_openai_compatible(), parse_number(), parse_choice(), parse_json_field()
Import results from elsewhere as_msa_runs(), msa_counts()
Variance components, numeric / ordinal / binary msa_fit()
Gauge R&R statistics and verdict msa_grr(), msa_boot()
Attribute agreement, accuracy msa_agreement() (Krippendorff’s alpha, Cohen’s kappa)
Bias and linearity msa_bias()
Robustness screening pb_design(), msa_robustness() (Lenth’s PSE)
Study size by simulation msa_simulate(), msa_plan()
Ongoing system suitability msa_control_chart() (Westgard rules)
Validation report msa_report()

The vignette (vignette("llmsa")) runs a complete validation offline with the mock backend.

Design notes

  • Replicates must be spread in time. Thinking Machines Lab showed in 2025 that identical prompts at temperature 0 return different completions because batch composition on the server changes the arithmetic. Five calls within one second underestimate repeatability; use blocks and run them on different days.
  • Few levels, wide intervals. Three models and four prompt variants are three and four levels of a random effect. Their variance components are estimated with large uncertainty and fits are often singular. Report bootstrap intervals (msa_boot()) and plan the study (msa_plan()); the number of prompt variants, not the number of items, drives the precision of the reproducibility estimate.
  • Memorisation confounds accuracy, not precision. Reference answers that are public (ClinVar, textbooks) may be in the training data. Use items added after the model’s cut-off for the accuracy question; the precision statistics are unaffected.
  • Acceptance criteria follow model risk. The AIAG thresholds (10 % and 30 % of study variation) are defaults, not laws. Set them from the consequence of a wrong decision in the stated context of use.
  • Free-text outcomes judged by a second model are a second measurement system that needs its own validation (a nested MSA). This release covers numeric, ordinal and binary outcomes.

Roadmap

  • Batched multi-item prompts: position and carry-over effects analysed as in a crossover study (Williams designs).
  • Nested validation of LLM-as-judge scoring for free-text outcomes.
  • Bootstrap intervals for ordinal fits; modified-large-sample intervals for variance components.
  • Detection-limit style experiments: how much evidence must a document contain before a finding is extracted reliably.
